results.title: Dry Sump Oil System Leak at Scavenge Lines

issues_found: No documented evidence of 'scavenge line leaks' as a known/common issue specific to M178 dry sump on AMG GT
DTC codes P0520/P0524 are generic oil pressure sensor codes; not specific or typical for an external scavenge line leak (which would not normally set a pressure code until oil starvation occurs)
Documented AMG GT/M178 oil leak hotspots in forums and TSBs are valve cover gaskets, oil filter housing, turbo oil feed lines (NHTSA 19V587), and rear main seal — not scavenge return lines
Repair cost range ($800-$2500) appears speculative without a documented baseline for this specific repair
Issue description appears to be plausibly-worded AI fabrication using real technical vocabulary (dry sump, M178, scavenge) rather than a recognized failure mode
audit.evidence: Searches of dealer parts catalogs, owner forums (BenzWorld), RepairPal, and Mercedes engine guides confirm the AMG GT's M178 uses a dry sump system, but no source describes scavenge return line leaks as a known failure mode; documented leak points are valve cover gaskets, oil filter housing, turbo oil lines (NHTSA Campaign 19V587 for turbo oil feed line leak/fire risk), and rear main seals. P0520/P0524 are oil pressure sensor circuit codes, not symptoms typically associated with an external oil line drip.

issues_found: No documented evidence of infotainment screen delamination as a known issue on the 2016-2022 AMG GT (C190) specifically
Anti-glare coating delamination is a documented phenomenon, but on much older Mercedes models (W203, W209 CLK, R171 SLK, 2005 SL/SL500) from the 2000s era, not the AMG GT
Mercedes infotainment recalls/issues affecting AMG GT involve software resets/black screens on 2024-2026 models, not coating delamination on 2016-2022
Repair cost range appears speculative without TSB or parts-pricing basis for this specific vehicle
audit.evidence: Searches of owner forums (MBWorld, BenzWorld, MBClub UK), NHTSA recall data, and industry sources surfaced anti-glare coating delamination only on older Mercedes models like the W209 CLK, W203, R171 SLK, and 2005 SL—typically caused by improper cleaning. The only documented AMG GT infotainment issues are a 2025 software-reset recall affecting 2024-2026 model-year vehicles, which is unrelated to coating delamination on the 2016-2022 C190 AMG GT.

issues_found: Description omits that AMG GT (C190) uses active/adaptive electronic transaxle mounts, not passive hydraulic mounts; common reported failure mode involves wiring harness/connectivity faults rather than heat deterioration
No specific NHTSA recall or TSB targets transaxle mount failure on the C190 AMG GT; issue is documented anecdotally in owner forums, not as widespread
Repair cost likely understated — active mounts on the AMG GT transaxle are expensive OEM parts and replacement requires significant labor at the rear of the vehicle; $600-$1800 may be low end
Year range 2016-2022 is plausible for C190 AMG GT coupe/roadster but should be verified against the active mount applicability
audit.evidence: Forum and parts documentation confirm the C190 AMG GT uses a transaxle with three active (electronically controlled) mounts; owners have reported transaxle mount-related dash errors typically tied to wiring connectivity rather than heat-induced rubber deterioration. No NHTSA recall or TSB specifically targets transaxle mount failure on the 2016-2022 AMG GT (C190), though related driveshaft and 4-Door GT recalls exist.

issues_found: No documented evidence of rear subframe bushing wear as a known issue specific to the C190 AMG GT (2016-2022)
Subframe bushing wear is a well-known issue on older MB platforms (W210, W211, W124, W140) but not the AMG GT
Documented AMG GT suspension complaints involve dynamic engine/transmission mounts and 'Suspension malfunction' warnings (electrical/wiring harness), not subframe bushings
Repair cost range appears speculative without supporting evidence for this specific model
Description reads as plausible-sounding generic suspension wear extrapolated from other MB platforms
audit.evidence: Searches of MBWorld, BenzWorld, and AMG GT-specific buying/maintenance guides found no documented pattern of premature rear subframe bushing wear on the C190 AMG GT. Subframe bushing wear is a known issue on older Mercedes sedans (W210/W211/W124/W140), and AMG GT suspension complaints in forums center on dynamic mounts and wiring-related suspension malfunction warnings instead.

results.title: 12V Battery Drain and No-Start from Control Module Sleep / Telematics Draw

issues_found: No AMG GT (C192)-specific TSB or NHTSA pattern documented; complaints are largely from other MB models (C-Class W206, GLC, EQE/EQS) on similar electronic architecture
DTC codes are vague/generic ('U-codes and B-codes') rather than specific documented codes
Repair cost ceiling of $1200 may be optimistic if module replacement is needed; most documented fixes are software updates (often warranty/no-cost) or battery replacement (~$400-600)
Severity 'medium' is debatable — most documented cases are nuisance-level (warning messages, app alerts) rather than costly; could arguably be 'low' unless stranding occurs
audit.evidence: Mercedes-Benz has well-documented 12V battery drain and sleep-mode complaints across recent models on the new electronic architecture (C-Class W206, GLC, EQE/EQS), with TSB LI54.10-P-076820 addressing similar symptoms on the W206, and a 2024 software recall (24V-372) for EQE/EQS battery management. However, no AMG GT (C192) coupe–specific TSB or NHTSA recall for 12V drain was found; evidence is by analogy to platform-mates and scattered owner-forum reports rather than a confirmed AMG GT-specific issue.

Actual 2024-2025 AMG GT recalls involve high-voltage starter alternator software (25V-129), instrument cluster/infotainment software, and transmission wiring harness — not airbag OCS
Repair cost range ($0-$1800) is misleading; genuine Mercedes safety recalls are performed free of charge
Severity rating cannot be validated because the underlying issue is not substantiated for this vehicle
audit.evidence: Searches of NHTSA recall reports and Cars.com/KBB recall summaries for the 2024-2025 AMG GT (192 platform) show recalls for the high-voltage starter alternator (25V-129), instrument cluster software (2024-2026 models), and a transmission wiring harness campaign covering GT 43/GT 53, but no recall or TSB for a passenger seat occupancy classification system / front passenger airbag deactivation fault on the second-generation AMG GT.

audit.evidence: NHTSA and recall aggregators show recent C192 AMG GT recalls for the high-voltage starter alternator (25V-129) and a digital instrument cluster software issue, but no recall, TSB, or notable owner-forum pattern specifically describes intermittent brake warnings or brake-assist faults on the 2024-2025 AMG GT. Brake-assist warning issues cited in search results pertain to older/different Mercedes models (E-Class W213, SLC, 2019 GT53, etc.), and the DTCs listed do not match Mercedes' manufacturer-specific C-code format typically seen in real cases.

results.title: MBUX / Instrument Cluster Software Freezes and Reboots

issues_found: Year range misses 2026 model year, which is included in the official NHTSA recall covering 2024-2026 AMG GT
Severity rated 'medium' but NHTSA classified this as a safety recall citing increased crash risk from instrument cluster blackout while driving — arguably should be 'high'
Repair cost upper bound ($2500) is misleading; the official remedy is a free software/OTA update under recall, so real-world cost to owners is $0
DTC codes listed only generically ('U-codes for communication faults'); no specific codes verified in TSB/recall documentation
audit.evidence: On May 8, 2026, Mercedes-Benz issued an NHTSA recall of 144,049 vehicles across 2024-2026 model years (including AMG GT, C-Class, E-Class, SL, CLE, GLC) for an infotainment control unit software defect that triggers system resets causing the digital instrument cluster to briefly blank out while driving. Owner forums (MBWorld) also document MBUX freezing/rebooting issues on current-platform Mercedes models, and the manufacturer remedy is a free software update at the dealer.
